conviction_note: Evidence roughly offsets. The June exit rate ($24m a month, so about $72m a quarter) sits above the one aggregator Q3 revenue bar ($68.7m) and inside the company's own FY guide, which implies $68-83m a quarter. Against it: a credit-loss allowance at 26% of gross receivables, a competitor (ORGO) that cut its guide hard after MDXG last spoke, and the FTC second request delaying Sanara. Last quarter's revenue beat closed +0.95% after gapping down, so p_up is held near 50 (51) while abs_move stays above the 6.44% median, at 8.0, because this is the first quarter after the cost cuts and the FY range may be narrowed.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $68.7m and EPS $0.01 (Benzinga forecast table, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MDXG/earnings-forecasts); AAII has next-quarter EPS at -$0.01 from 2 analysts; Earnings Whispers (2026-10-20, https://finviz.com/news/405228/mimedx-must-show-its-wound-care-rebound-outlasted-a-strong-june) says no reliable consensus exists. So the street bar has ONE source and is disputed. The company bar: FY2026 net sales $260-290m reiterated 2026-07-29 (https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/mimedx-announces-second-quarter-2026-operating-financial-results). H1 was $123.4m, so H2 needs $136.6-166.6m, about $68-83m a quarter, midpoint about $76m. The $68.7m street number sits at the guide's low end. Sizes on the street bar are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 9.4M shares, about 7.3 days to cover, at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, down from 10.8M / 10.9 days at 09-15 (Curved Trading via search snippet, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/mdxg/short-interest/, page returned 403 to fetch, so snippet_only). That is about 6.4% of 145.8M shares outstanding (10-Q). Equibles had 5.79% of float at 2026-08-20. Moderately short, not crowded. No usable option chain: unusable_chain, total OI 34, put/call OI 0.7, no skew. Tape: spot $3.95, 20-day -15.2%, 5-day +5.6%, 50% off the 52-week high. The stock was $4.67 on 10-10 and $4.38 on 10-20, then fell 8.4% to $3.88 on 10-21 with no cause found.

findings.finding: Management said on the 2026-07-29 call that June was the highest month of 2026 at $24M and that sales grew sequentially in each month of Q2. Holding June flat gives about $72M for Q3, against the $68.7M aggregator consensus (+4.8%). The FY guide of $260-290M needs about $68-83M a quarter in H2. Management called July momentum 'good' and declined to give numbers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $64.4M beat the $63.5M consensus and the guide was reiterated; the stock gapped down, then closed +0.95% (baseline 2026-07-29). Q1 2026 (2026-04-29): +8.74% in the baseline. Revenue beats have been bought weakly.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's $68.7M sits at the guide's low end, below a flat June run-rate, and the stock fell about 15% over 20 days into the print. If the run-rate were priced, consensus would sit near $72-76M and the stock would not be trading near its post-Q2 low. But the beat lands inside what the company already guided to, and the bar has one source.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-10-20 (https://finviz.com/news/405228/mimedx-must-show-its-wound-care-rebound-outlasted-a-strong-june): a Q3 in the low $70Ms keeps the outlook on track, and wound-centre volume was +44% sequentially. That preview draws on the same call, so this is the same document read twice, not an independent source.

findings.finding: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was -$8M (-13% of sales), but management said results trended near breakeven by June. It guided gross margin back to the mid-70s from Q3 (Q2 GAAP 69%, adjusted about 74%) and Q4 adjusted EBITDA to high single digits of revenue. It also said it expects no significant further bad debt in H2 after a $5M Q2 charge. EPS consensus is $0.01 or -$0.01.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Q2, EPS of -$0.05 missed -$0.03 while revenue beat; the stock gapped down (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/mimedx-group-nasdaqmdxg-shares-gap-down-on-disappointing-earnings-2026-07-30/). A profitability miss has been punished at the open.
findings.why_not_priced: This is mostly guided, so it is mostly priced. The open question is whether the roughly $40M of cost cuts shows up as a positive adjusted EBITDA quarter one quarter early. An EPS bar of about zero means a small positive print would read as a beat.
findings.independence: Q2 press release, same day (https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/mimedx-announces-second-quarter-2026-operating-financial-results): 'path back to profitability for the second half'. Same company source.

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q shows receivables strain. Gross AR fell to $56.1M from $84.4M while the credit-loss allowance rose to $14.8M from $8.7M, so the allowance is 26% of gross AR. Credit-loss expense was $5.3M in Q2 against $0.4M a year earlier, attributed to 'credit deterioration of certain legacy customers'. On the call, management described MACs as behind on claims processing and audits and clawbacks as rising, which keeps up the risk of another charge in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 bad-debt charge contributed to the EPS miss that gapped the stock down on 2026-07-30 before it closed +0.95%.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews and consensus focus on the wound volume rebound, and management told the market not to expect significant further charges. A 26% allowance alongside MAC payment delays at customers is a 10-Q detail that previews do not carry. If it were priced, EPS consensus would sit below zero rather than at $0.01.
findings.independence: Burr & Forman on rising UPIC recoupments (https://www.burr.com/newsroom/articles/wound-care-and-skin-substitute-investigations-and-recoupments-increase-drastically) and the HFMA piece of 2026-07-13 on the fraud takedown (https://www.hfma.org/payment-reimbursement-and-managed-care/medicare-skin-substitute-reimbursement/). These are industry proxies.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-15/16 the FTC issued Second Requests to MiMedx and Sanara MedTech on the $350M Sanara deal. That extends the HSR waiting period to 30 days after substantial compliance and likely pushes closing past the 'by year-end' target. The deal is funded by a $300M Hayfin term loan at SOFR+6.25%. The call will carry the first timing update; the stock fell 2.8% on the news.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Deal announced with Q2 on 2026-07-29: the stock gapped down and closed +0.95%. Second Request on 2026-10-16: MDXG -2.8%, SMTI -5.5% (Stocktwits).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is public and the stock reacted. What is not priced is the new closing date and whether the combined '>$400M 2027 revenue at >20% EBITDA margin' framing is restated. On the financing question: the money buys about $100M of trailing revenue at a gross margin above 90% plus $20M of synergies, so it is not distress, and a delay mainly costs time and deal certainty.
findings.independence: MiMedx 8-K item 8.01 filed 2026-10-16 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001376339/000121390026110041/0001213900-26-110041-index.htm) and the Sanara 8-K of 2026-10-15. Same event, different filers.

findings.finding: Peer Organogenesis reported on 2026-08-06, after MDXG last spoke. Q2 net product revenue was $42.8M against $100.8M a year earlier, advanced wound care was -61%, the FY2026 guide was cut to $179-215M from $270-310M, cash fell to $47M, and an equity offering followed. The stock was about $1.29 on 10-09. MDXG's own wound line was also -61% y/y in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No MDXG history on peer read-throughs found. MDXG closed +0.95% on its own Q2, a week before the ORGO cut.
findings.why_not_priced: The read cuts both ways and the net is small. A deepening H2 contraction in Medicare skin-substitute wound care argues against MDXG's wound rebound, while a distressed competitor losing accounts could send share to MDXG. Netted against the rest of the company: wound is now about 39% of MDXG sales, and surgical (61%, +15% y/y) is untouched by ORGO's problem. If the market had extended ORGO's cut to MDXG, the street bar would sit below the guide's low end; it sits at it.
findings.independence: Panabee summary of the ORGO Q2 print, 2026-08-06 (https://www.panabee.com/news/organogenesis-earnings-q3-2026). The URL mislabels it Q3; the content is Q2 2026. It is a proxy: a competitor, not MDXG's own number.

findings.finding: Into the print: short interest of 9.4M shares (about 6.4% of 145.8M shares, about 7.3 days to cover at the 09-30 settlement, down from 10.8M), and the stock down 15% over 20 days. Retail sentiment is bearish (Stocktwits, 10-16). That is a modest asymmetry toward covering on any clean quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 5 of 7 prior prints were up (baseline), median absolute move 6.44%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price itself, so this is weak by construction. The late-October drawdown has no identified cause, and the absence of a cause is given zero weight. Only the measured short position is sized.
findings.independence: Equibles: 5.79% of float short, 5.3 days to cover, at 2026-08-20 (https://equibles.com/stocks/mdxg/shortinterest).

outside_window.finding: The CMS CY2027 Physician Fee Schedule final rule, which sets whether the flat $127/cm2 skin-substitute rate continues into 2027 as proposed, typically publishes around 31 Oct - 2 Nov. That is after the 2026-10-29 close.
Organogenesis Q3 results on 2026-11-05 and Sanara Q3 on about 2026-11-10: peer read-throughs after the window.
Substantial compliance with the FTC Second Request and Sanara closing: likely 2027 rather than year-end.

baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with. The evidence leans mildly positive on revenue against a bar at the guide's low end and a stock down 15% into the print, offset by credit-quality and peer negatives; net about zero, which matches a baseline with no priced direction.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6: the run-rate beat lands inside the company's own guided H2 range, and the street bar has one disputed source; finding 1 cut from +1.5 to +1.0, print_vs_bar from +5 to +4.
Lesson 1 and 6: profitability path is explicitly guided (mid-70s GM, Q4 high-single-digit EBITDA margin); finding 2 cut from +0.5 to +0.3; p_up from 52 to 51 because the Q2 beat was sold at the open.
Lesson 7: short interest is moderate (about 6.4%, 7.3 days); the receivables negative was trimmed from -1.0 to -0.8.
Lesson 9 and 5: the ORGO read-through is a wound-only proxy against a company 61% surgical; cut from -0.8 to -0.5.
Lesson 5: an unexplained drawdown is worth 0; the positioning finding was cut from +0.4 to +0.2 and now rests on short interest alone.

Lesson 4: financing question answered (the loan buys a 90%+ gross-margin, about $100M-revenue surgical business plus $20M synergies; not distress); the FTC finding was left at -0.3 as a timing risk, not a distress sign.
